The five of you, who have been adventuring and traveling together for the better part of this last year, have been hired by a minor lord named Holda, the second son of a no-name lord from southern Sembara. He spent the last twenty-five years or more as an adventurer and sellsword, always trying to find and make his fortune and never quite succeeding. Last spring, after killing a dragon that had come down from the north, losing his entire party in the process, and discovering that, since it was a wandering dragon, there was no hoard, he found himself with nothing more in his purse than he had three decades ago when he left home. He was drinking his misery away when a long-lived elf approached him and gave him the deed to a...

lines.speaker: DM

You were hired by Alden, a small, stout, pale human with a curiosity about you all and a profound fear of fire, apparently, to go there. Over several days, you journeyed upriver and then crossed through the forest, which grew denser, older, wilder, and less inhabited the farther you went. At last you came to Dandelion House, a marvel of late Drankorian architecture at least seven hundred years old, and a funny combination of both glorious and decrepit. Parts of it...

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: The windows and wooden window frames were decayed away into powder, as was much of the furniture inside, but not all of it. There must be some sort of preservation magic woven through the structure. Despite the misgivings of various party members, you met Lord Holda: proud, bitter, resentful, over the hill, not in a cliched sort of way, but with the sense that his best days were behind him and they were not that great anyway. He seemed stuck on a wheel, always turning, one year after the next, always different but always the same. He told you the story of this self-described elven archivist, who gave him a deed to the house, its lands, and all the treasures therein, on the condition that Holda step through a door in the floor and convince a man beyond to end a long-held treaty.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Holda, whose only negotiation strategy, and maybe his only strategy for moving through the world, seems to be intimidation, failed immediately to convince the man on the other side of this door of anything and turned to the party for help. Tarek, reading the document, knew that something did not fit. Kaito, by this point, had gone from deep fear bordering on paranoia to excitement bordering on rapturous enthusiasm. Ayveen observed that ending an unknown treaty may not be a wise course of action, and Txarro pointed out that the treasure could equally well be a trap or a metaphor. Nonetheless, the party arose before dawn, woken by the grandfather clock, still in fine condition. Alden collected you from your rooms, led you down through the ground floor, down through a massive basement, and down further still, opening a locked door with a glowing gold key. He led you down through a passage hewn from living rock into a root-covered subcellar that surely predates the entire manor above it. On reflection, subcellar is not even quite the right word. You assumed that at the moment, given its position below the cellar, but there was nothing in it except walls covered entirely in massive, hollowed-out roots.

Just as he closed the door behind you, Tarek realized the unsettling thing about the contract: it was four hundred years old, but written in contemporary Sembaran. We open in that moment, illuminated by a couple of light spells, as the five of you are crawling single file through this tunnel, barely bigger than you, making your way toward who knows what.

The road continues to the gate, which is right off the road maybe a quarter mile ahead. There are two guards there, or you assume they are guards because they are in the position and place of guards. But if they are, they are awfully casual about it. There are two long spears leaning behind them. They are not armored; they are dressed more like servants, in waistcoats, short pants, and soft leather boots. They do not have an especially intimidating look.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: They are not in a military posture. Yeah, go ahead.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: No, but it is more like... not the concierge, but a little more... I mean, they are not greeters, but they are...

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yeah, exactly. The gates are open behind them, so they are not guarding in that way. The gate is set into the hedgerow.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: Now I am kind of like, should we just go?

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: Can I tell if these are humans, elves? What do they look like?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: I do not think the owl can tell at that distance. They are human-sized mostly, but some are smaller. You see a pair of halflings walking across the lawn, probably an elf or two sprinkled in there.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: Kaito is just like, "Let's go. Do not worry about this."

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: He starts walking confidently ahead, rearranges his stuff so he looks straight, and says, "Let's go."

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: I will send the owl to fly by over the manor house, staying about 120 feet up or so.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Try to be...

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: Pretty quiet on the wing. It will try to be stealthy, depending on the darkness, hard to see against the sky.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Stirring.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: Circle over the manor house, get a better look at who these people might be, see if I can get a rough count of how many people there are, and see whether everybody is just milling around or if there is some order to the party.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Are there guards at the manor house gate? Basic whatever-the-owl-can-figure-out, and then fly back. Your impression is that the guards at the gate are formal. While there are people who are armed in the party, it is dress arms: the saber someone in a cavalry officer's uniform is wearing, or the long knives that elves...

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: Kaito is hustling now. He's like, "Guys, the party is ending. We have to get there now."

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: What's your story, Kaito?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Do not worry. Money comes to him.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: Faith.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: Thank you.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: Are you going alone?

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: Anybody wants to come with me? Let's just say Tarek, for sure, would come. Tarek and Kaito, this is kind of their thing. Tarek is down for this. This is common...

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Like...

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: This is a good moment.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: So you are going up to the gate? Alright.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: Is anybody else coming, or do you guys...

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: I mean...

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: Is there a reason for us not to all go?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yeah, let's all stay together. Just as a default posture of paranoia, right?

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: Other than the fact that Augury did not say all of us marching up to the gate was good.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: But maybe we do not introduce ourselves and immediately ask to speak to the Lord of the Manor.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: No, no, no. A treaty. Yeah, sorry.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: On that part, let's not say any of that stuff. Just so you know, we have done this enough now together as a group: in a situation like this, Kaito and Tarek are going to go.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: They are not necessarily going to make a scene, but Kaito is a glamour bard. He is immediately trying to figure out where the other performers are, so he can start building a little connection with some of the people there, set some vibes, and see if he can attract interesting people over. The goal here is that we do not say anything out loud about what we are here for yet, but...

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Let's just feel it out and see.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: I do not think there is anything here that is going to kill us right away.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: What do you guys think?

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: The owl overhead.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: As you are coming up to the gate, the last thing you see through the owl's eyes, just before the guards notice you, stand, rub their eyes, and raise a hand to hail you, is a tall figure stepping into one of the manor doors, illuminated brightly from behind. A man? He moves with a lithe grace like a dancer. With the backlighting, it is difficult to tell if the smoothness of his face is his face itself or a masquerade-like mask he has been putting on. You see him scan over the crowd. His eyes fall away down the slope of the hills to where people are climbing into the rowboat to head onward. He notes sharp voices raised among a small cluster of people below the patios. Then he looks directly at the owl, makes eye contact, nods to himself, and steps back inside the house. The guards raise a hand in greeting, but then a look of confusion comes over their faces. They are two deeply wrinkled elderly men, pot-bellied, wearing the sort of separate hood from a cloak.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: They look at you with a note of confusion, then lift their noses and sniff, almost dog-like. In their sniffing, there is a strange moment when you do not understand if you are seeing men pretending to be dogs or dogs pretending to be men. Then they finish, nod a greeting, and say, "Well met and welcome, mortals."

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: What?

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: Word dope.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Well met and welcome, mortals.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: Kaito gives a flourish of his cape.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: What language do they say this in?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Common. Heavily accented Common.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: Accented Common?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Ambiguously accented Common.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: Kaito gives a flourish. Greetings.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: Before he walks in, he glances and says, "The festivities ending soon?"

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Indeed. Indeed. The party is ending. You're just in time.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "The party before it ends," says one, with a chuckle. "Indeed, my favorite time. Where have you come from? It is unusual to see so many of you together at once at this time of night."

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: Do we use Detect Thoughts now?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Find out in a minute. No, not now.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: Where did we come from? Down the road, of course.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: The one who has not said anything so far chuckles, like you have made a very incisive joke.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: And may I ask, can you share more about the party?

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: Well, our apologies for being late.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "I will tell you this. We belong to the road, not to the party. The party is not our story. We know what we hear and smell and see through the gate, but this is as far as we go."

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: Well, perhaps some candor. We came from the road. We saw bodies.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: Presumably coming from here.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "Maybe, maybe not. I love a good party."

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: Kaito gives another flourish and a wink. But also, the bodies. Anything you might be able to share about the party?

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: And the Lord here?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: The ones you passed did not come from this house. But further up the road.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: Is there anything further up the road? I mean, the road keeps going, right?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yes, the road absolutely keeps going. The road goes on and on and on. In the Twilight Kingdom, there are a dozen dozen houses, homes, and holes, with the setting sun just over the horizon.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: This is the Twilight Kingdom.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: Which.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Which way is the road going? Toward the sun? Away from it? As near as you can tell, the road runs parallel to what in any other place would be the north-south axis, exactly between day and night. You notice, in fact, having been here for at least an hour now, that the sun has not moved in the sky. Sensing your confusion, the same guard says, "Do you have, where you are from, disease that spreads from one person to another?"

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "Well, we do not have that here. But we have something similar. Sometimes people get infected in a way. Sometimes people get caught by a bad smell. That smell can cause disaster and spread to more people with the bad smell. We belong to the road. We keep the road safe. Sometimes, with the people who have the bad smell, you cannot get the bad smell out of them any other way. I think that is what you saw."

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: They only have spears, they don't have any bows or anything like that.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Though their feet are shod in plain, soft boots.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: So, the bodies. You guys do not have anything to do with the bodies.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "My people do. Some of us stay at the gate, some of us travel the road."

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: But you do not know what to do with the bodies?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: The two of us? No. No, no. Our place is the gate.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: Right. And again, the Lord of the manor here? What do you know of him?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "He came to the gate once, just at the height of the party, just before... you know what it is like when a gathering starts to come apart? You can feel it before anyone has even left. He came in that moment to tell us to be careful of travelers on the road, to smell very carefully for the bad smell, but to let in any mortal who wanted entrance. It was a strange thing. I remember it, too. I would have thought he just said any guest who wanted entrance, but he said any mortal who wants entrance, send them in."

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: Excellent.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: When was this directive?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "Just as the party began to end. Just after the height of it. We arrived, of course, when it was just beginning."

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: Oh, so quite recently. How long has this party been going?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: He shakes his head, confused, like you are asking a ridiculous question. "It began and reached its peak, and now it is coming apart."

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: Yeah, yeah, yeah, no, I understand.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: You mentioned the other lords down the road. Tensions?

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: Well, you just said the bodies, they're not from here, they're not from this house, the bodies are from another house.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "Do you know what house they are from? There is a house that, when people come out of it, they sometimes come out with the bad smell."

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: What does that smell like, so we can avoid it?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: He looks thoughtful for a second, then locks eyes with you and says, "It smells exactly unlike anything else I have ever smelled in my entire living. It is the opposite of smell."

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: That is confusing. Thank you.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: He gives a nod.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: Are there other mortals with this party?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "There are a handful. A few have come by boat. The halflings came soon after it began. They always seem to. I think there was a dwarf..." He turns to the other one. "The dwarf went in. Did they come out? And a few I could not quite tell. None of them had the bad smell, though."

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: Did any come and go?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "Any number of them have come and gone."

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: Since the party began to end?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: He looks thoughtful for a moment, as though trying to put that together for the first time. "Let's see. Yes. They have been going more than coming lately, I suppose."

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: That is what ending means, right?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Would you like to go in?

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: The house down at the end of the road, the one that's kind of fallen apart.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: He says, in a language you do not recognize, what must surely be some curse, and spits. "It is a bad-smelling place. We do not go there."

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: Does the road end in the other direction, too?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "Roads do not end. They only ever go on and on."

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: No, some roads do not... Edric covers his mouth, like, I probably should not get in an argument with them, and stops talking.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: We belong to the road, he says. We know.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: Should we go in? Txarro says to everybody else in Tollish, not Common, which I presume everybody understands.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: Let's do it.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: We would like to enter.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Very good. Did you bring gifts?

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: I was literally going to say that at the very beginning. Unfortunately, gifts are a relative term. Something I possess may be a gift to some and may not be to others. So we come bearing our possessions. To the extent that some of those may be worthy and deemed gifts, then we have them.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: You will not like that. Collectively, do we have anything nice? Classic things one might think of as a gift?

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: I have some water blessed by the Night Queen.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Let's do this.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: Song of a loon? Have you heard a loon call before?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: No. What is that?

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: A gift for the Lord of the Manor.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Very good.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: Would he approve of me sharing my gifts with you?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "Listen. I am bribable. Tell me this instead, and I will let you through. It has been so long since I have gotten to speak with anyone who dreams. What did you dream of last time you slept?"

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: Amazing.

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: Didn't one of us have a very weird nightmare about the...

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Lord of the Manor? This is completely open to whatever you would like to do with it.

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: I mean, I am happy to make up a dream. I am just wondering, didn't...

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: One of us actually describe a dream about...

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: The manor, in that session?

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: Yeah, I think that was Edric.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Trying to remember my memories.

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: Hmm.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: Maybe not, I don't know.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Dreams, well...

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: Most of my dreams are of animals, which you seem to have few of here.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: Have you heard of... I am trying to think of an interesting bird that would live in Tollen. A bittern.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: No. What do they smell like?

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: Fishy and wet.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Hmm.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: And of mud and reeds.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Mmm.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: I dreamt of one wandering, lost, through a marsh, calling its low, hooting noise, trying to find... what, I don't know.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: But as it reached the edge of the reeds and came out of the water onto the mud, it began to burrow and dig. As it did, it turned into a snake and slithered through the dirt, shedding its skin as it went, which grew into reeds. Then it came to the water again and sprouted feathers from its now-bare skin, growing into a bittern again, calling a low, moaning noise.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Was the bird at the end the same or different from the bird at the beginning?

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: Both.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "Very good." And he is not satisfied.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: I didn't...

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Or are you satisfied? "Listen, I do not mean to be greedy. But it is a precious opportunity. I have always wondered what it is like. What do you make of these things?"

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: Edric says, "I normally dream of baking bread. Just the smell of it."

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "Mmm. I know that smell. That is a good smell."

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: But then sometimes there is the other dream.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: But maybe I shouldn't speak of it here.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: He kind of rumbles. "Hmm. I am curious now, though. What is this other dream? You make it sound like it is unchosen. You do not get to choose your dreams."

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: No. But dreams come from the gods. You do not know that?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "I do not dream. I only smell."

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: Well, there is the one...

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: Where I'm lying in a grave.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "Oof. Not enough. What is the..."

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: It's always the same.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: Great dream again.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: And then...

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: A crown appears.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: Six points of light, coming through the dirt.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: And I am small. I cannot move on my own very well, I can only crawl. The crown gets brighter and brighter, and I know to follow it.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: I think it might be a memory, in a way.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: It might be a what?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: A memory, in a way.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: Whoa, memory.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: And then the grave dissolves. Then I wake up.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "When you are in the grave, is it open to the sky, or are you under dirt?"

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: No, it's...

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: It is dirt until the light starts to... the six points of light start to melt it away.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: Almost like, like a beam, like...

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Edric waves his hand, and a ball of light appears. He closes his fist, and it goes away again. But six of them, like a crown, tunneling their way through. The guard nods. "Grave smell is a good smell. Like a bath, it cleans. It is good that you are in the grave, sometimes."

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: Have you never smelled a bad grave smell?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Once I smelled the bad smell for the first time, nothing else was bad anymore, except for it.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: Sorry, where's the bad smell come from again?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "Bad smell comes from the mortals who catch it."

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: Do any of the mortals here have it?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "No. No one inside these grounds does. That is what we are here for: to sniff it out and keep it from entry."

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: One more dream, and I'll let you through.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: Yeah, I will tell you a dream. But before I do, Kaito pulls out his lute and another instrument, a small flute. He gives both of them a quick little flourish with incredible skill. Not too showy, just enough to show that this guy can definitely play these things.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Give me a Performance roll.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Solid.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: Does the Lord of the Manor appreciate skill in song, in music?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "Presumed so, as gifts anyway. I do not know. It is a good offer to make."

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: Dreams. You know, I find my dreams are never one thing.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: The dreams are always one thing connected into another thing, into another.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: Elves do not dream.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: What's that?

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: They don't sleep.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: What's that?

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: Owls don't drink.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: Elves do not dream. Elves do not sleep.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Oh, shit.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: Oh, that sucks.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Oh well.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: Alright, I do not answer this question now.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: Elves spend the first, like, 50 years of their life dreaming.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: Can I share one of those?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yeah, okay.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: There is no lore about what it is at all, so totally...

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yeah. Who knows?

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: Who knows what happens, all we know is...

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: Perfect. Let me say this later, then.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: Well, my kind, we effectively have one dream, and it only happens once. So I actually share your nostalgia. For you, I guess it is a curiosity, since you have never had a dream. But for me, it is more nostalgia, because I have only ever had one. But if you like, I can share some snippets of that dream.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "Tell me."

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: It was the one dream, and it was a long dream. The parts I am most nostalgic for are less one moment or one narrative and more a whole bunch of scenes clipped and chopped and strewn together, almost like a patchwork quilt made of so many different colors and shapes and textures and smells.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: It would go from one scene with massive trees of unimaginable size, swaying huge roots, large craggy grass, and the feeling of something so raw and alive.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: And then all of a sudden, nothingness in the night sky, just black.

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: Except stars, everywhere, and then shifting from stars to blackness. Then all of a sudden, waves are crashing over your head, and you are in a boat rocking up and down, your body swaying back and forth. Then you feel like you are in the middle of the ocean, except you are not. You are in the middle of a fire, in a flame inside a fireplace. It is raging hot, and you are sweating, and it is incredibly uncomfortable, until you hear the sound of a voice singing. It is your siblings, except do you have siblings or not in real life? It is hard to say. The voices are so golden and beautiful and piercing, and they pull you out of the fire. The next thing you know, you look down and you are a bird, or maybe not even a bird, but you are flying. You can see, hundreds of feet below, maybe miles below, just spots of houses and buildings. It goes on and on like that. I will never have another one, but the one was pretty good, and I like that I can go back and visit parts of it.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "I suspect sometimes that the lord of this house, too, lives always with a sense of having lost something that will not come back again. Not just something that will not come back again, but something that can never come back again."

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: Wait, say that last part again?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "That the Lord of this house lives having lost something, like you, that he cannot ever recover again."

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: Mmm...

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "But I do not hear you describing it as loss or grief. I hear acceptance of that change."

lines.speaker: Kaito Min
lines.text: No regrets, no remorse. Onwards.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: It is what it is. Kit, I do not want to cut you off if you have one lined up, but I am also happy to move us in.

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: I got flummoxed by the elves-don't-dream thing. I had something to say to...

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: You know, full...

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: third one, so we have it as needed, but I am fine.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: They gesture for you to step through the gate.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: You see the long, sloping lawn that leads from the river's edge up to the patios and open doors of a bright and handsome house. String lights are strung in globes down the hill as the ground falls away ahead of you. You see groups of ones and twos and fours and fives. You see the signs of a party ending. The lighting is strange and uneven: some rooms are brightly lit, some less so. On a second glance, many of the lanterns have already gone out, and in others, the candles are flickering low. You want to give him a hug, but you should not give him a hug, because he is not the sort of person you give a hug to. If there is one thing you take away: just not the hugs. Does that answer your question?"

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: Come for a stroll with us. Let's find some wine and maybe clear your heads a bit.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: He allows himself to be persuaded and helps his friend up, too. They follow after you.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: I am happy to walk with them, but my main goal is to find... now I strongly suspect that everybody here has been here for far longer than they think. I want to find another...

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Human or mortal of some kind, probably not an elf. Yeah, so...

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: Have Edric and I run into anyone on our way to a fine wine?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yes, you see two obvious mortals. One is in the library, napping behind a couch in the space between the couch and the wall, possibly sleeping it off. Then, through an open archway into the room where a bar is set up along one corner, you see someone else. It is a funny intuition, because just looking at him, he is not a species you are familiar with, but you get the strong impression that he is both mortal and, more importantly at this party, sober. He is something like a tiger man, with the massive head of a Bengal tiger and the fur-covered, powerful body of a man.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Paws and a tail, wearing a waistcoat, a smoking jacket, silk pants, and smoking a pipe. What on earth about such a person would give us the impression that he is not fey?

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: Would the natural assumption be that this is a fey of some kind?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: You would, but there is something in the way he makes eye contact. If all of the other guests are, in a way, stuck in their own loops, captive to the moment of the party, there is a quality in which he is not. He is alert differently. Maybe he is fey, but the impression you get is: no.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: Where is he compared to the bar? Is he in the same room as them?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: You have come through a big entry ballroom, then through the library where you saw the sky, and then into this other room on the back side of the house, set up with the bar on one side and very picked-over food tables on the other. Big double doors in that room open onto another patio on the far side of the house. He is sitting in a chair out there. He notices you walking into the room with the bar and gives a little head nod in recognition.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: Not awkwardly, but I'm mostly focused on finding a bottle of wine for the halflings.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: The bar is unstaffed at this point in the night. Everywhere you look, in this room and the whole house, there are signs of this party ending. The tone of voice, even when you do not hear the words people are speaking, is a little sharper, a little less patient. None of the windows are open the same amount, because different people have opened them over the course of the night. There is a rug in the library folded over and not folded back down. The floor is sticky. Dirty dishes, wine glasses, and cutlery are everywhere, and the remains of the buffet have sat out too long. All the good things have been picked over. There is just broccoli left. The bar is unstaffed; you could certainly go behind and look for what is there.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: Yeah, sure.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: There is nothing still sealed, but there is one bottle that is a solid three-quarters full.

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: Edric, let's take a detour with that.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: They are...

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: The halflings will still be grateful for it if we delay a bit. I would like to meet this other guest.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Sure. Oh, man.

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: I walk into the room where he is and say, "I hope you do not mind our intruding in the quiet of this space."

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: This is the tiger-man smoking his pipe on the porch. In a deep voice, half purr and half gravel, he says, "Not at all, not at all." He gestures with his pipe to bring chairs. There is no one else out in this space. "Please, sit. Tell me your stories."

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: Have you had a chance to collect the stories of many of the guests at this gathering?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "Mmm. I have, but I will tell you a secret, because the two of you are also going to die. The thing that is most interesting to me is not the stories of the guests, but the stories of our host. By speaking to the guests, I have pieced together why this party is ending." He smiles a broad and extremely toothy grin. This is not a human-sized tiger head, but a massive one. He is seated, but he would probably be eight feet tall if he stood up.

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: Sounds like a very satisfactory mystery to have pieced together.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "I will say, I feel a bit smug."

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: I would not have all your hard work wasted. Perhaps you could give some hints.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Mmm.

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: So this delayed...

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Will you trade me for it?

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: I am not inclined to tell my stories when in a new place, where I am not sure of the practices. We are traveling together, Edric and I, and we have some stories.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Where are you from?

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: We're from Tollen.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Do you have a home there?

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: I do.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Allow me to stay in your home for a month and a day the next time I'm in Tollen.

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: Hmm. Is there a significance of that timing among your people? I've not met anyone like you before.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "No, it is mostly that I think I have about a month's worth of sights to see. It is a big city, after all."

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: Does it matter that I don't own the home?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Do you have a room of your own, undisturbed?

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Then I'll have that for a month and a day.

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: Well, it's unlikely that my parents would object.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "Very good." He reaches out a paw, easily four or five times the size of your own hand, to shake.

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: Edric, can you...

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: Kind of looking at you like, are you sure you want to do this?

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: I don't. I am asking you a question to distract from shaking this creature's hand. Edric, have you met my parents?

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: I... yes?

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: You would want me to ask their permission? Because I am sorry, sir, I am beginning to wonder if I ought to. And they are not...

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "It would be easier if I arrived as a man. I would be happy to."

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: I mean, some of my best friends look like all manner of animals, and... well, no, that is a wrong way of saying that. I have to say that a different way.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: He occupies himself, or has the affectation at least, of fiddling with his pipe and sprinkling in fresh tobacco from a pouch on his belt.

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: That is very thoughtful of you, to cover my blunders. I do not think it matters what you look like, sir.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Well, that's very open-minded of you.

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: Is there anything other than a stay in my parents' home, which I cannot grant, that I could offer you for a hint at your discovery?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Do you have any keys on your person?

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: I do not have any keys. But my friend probably has one. He tends to have interesting things in his pockets. I have not seen Tarek in a while.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: Tarek has gotta have a key on him.

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: Yeah, that's what I think.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "Very good. I will do it in exchange."

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: We do not know where he is.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Exactly.

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: Speak of the devil.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Tarek, how are you doing?

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: If he came in here with a key in his pocket, that would be perfect.

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: That was no fun. Oh, I missed that.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Oops. Real-life use of stealth, though, to get out of the room once they're finally asleep, which...

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: Come on, outside sides.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: You come into the party. You have talked to a couple of extremely drunk halflings who may have been in the Feywild for hundreds upon hundreds of years. Ayveen and Edric are on a back porch of the house, where they have stumbled into a Rakshasa, a giant tiger person smoking a pipe, who has told them that he has figured out the story of the Lord of the party, the Lord of the Manor here, and is willing to trade it. First he tried to get a stay in Ayveen's parents' home for a month and a day, but she seemed to decide that was a bad idea, and now he is asking for the key.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: So we are thinking Tarek might wander by with a key at this precise moment, since surely Tarek has keys in his pocket.

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: Preferably keys you do not care about, that belong to somebody else.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Tarek would never have keys.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: Own stuff.

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: Exactly.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yeah, of course Tarek has a set of keys.

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: Okay?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Tarek, as you cross through one of the rooms in the manor, he catches your eye and waves you over with an immense tiger paw. "Come, come. We were just speaking of you, I believe. Your friends have made a deal in your name. You have keys on you."

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: I have keys of many kinds.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "Mmm. Very good."

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: Allow me to share insight. Keys of wisdom. Keys to cryptograms.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "Choose three. I need keys for doors."

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: Tarek rummages around in his garments for a minute, patting his pockets.

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: Why, yes. Keys to the museum.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "Mmm. Very good." He brings his whole face very close, takes out a pair of spectacles and puts them on, and looks long and deep at each key. He picks three, for no discernible reason that you can tell, and slips them into his waistcoat pocket. He takes off his spectacles, sits back in his chair, takes a long puff from the pipe, and says, "Mmm. This is a delicious story. A delicious story. I came to the Twilight Kingdom, to the dozen dozen houses..."

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "Because there are certain things you can only find in twilight: things that have been lost and cannot be found again, places that can never be returned to. In my younger days, I got obsessive about that sort of time, that moment when all of the past has ended, but before the future has begun; the moment when things are beginning, but have not yet begun.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "I became, you might say, obsessive over this, and decided I would spend a day traveling the Twilight Kingdom. I pieced this together from the various guests. Most of the ones who are here now arrived at the party when it was just beginning, or arrived here too when it was in full swing, before..."

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "This." He gestures to the ineffable feeling of everything coming apart.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "At the height of the party, the neighbors who lived one house down the street came to the lord of this house, whose name was Lord Revel, Revel Beginning. They wanted from him a bargain, an agreement. They wanted him to do something for them: that any mortal who visited the party, sooner or later, would be sent through the front door of their house just up the road."

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "It is difficult to persuade a fey lord of anything at all. More difficult still to persuade him to do harm to his guests, which surely breaks one of the most basic rules of the dozen dozen houses. First they gave him things they found precious, the sort of things humans found precious: books from their library, a bird that could speak every language, a map of the stars that twilight had not yet revealed overhead.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "But for Lord Revel, this was of no consequence. Every guest brings gifts to his party, or," he says, chuckling and looking over you, "bribes the guards. So next, thinking that he wanted inspiration for his revelry, they gave him stories of human revelry: fireworks like rainbows above a city made entirely of towers and pyramids."

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "They told him about the ten days of celebration that followed the Emperor's coronation, and everything they saw there: performers from the endless ocean and beyond it. They told him stories of how the bonfires burned through the longest night on the floating cities far beyond the edge of the endless ocean.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "But none of these stories of revel were of any value, not to Lord Revel, who was himself revelry. And the dozen dozen houses of the Twilight Kingdom have celebrations for which there is no word in mortal tongue to describe them. So, in desperation, drawing on some book of lore they must have found, they challenged him instead to a game, to a contest: a game of poetry, a game of naming. Whoever could most beautifully name Lord Revel's estate could ask one favor of the other. Lord Revel went first."

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "And he spoke the name as it had been all evening long: Wide lawns spread down easy. Hanging lanterns welcome you. A party begins. Lord Revel Beginning.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "But this wizard guessed correctly that Revel was trapped inside his own story. Trapped, in fact, by his own immortality, trapped by the frozenness in time, unable to imagine that his story had any other moment in it except for the present. The wizard guessed correctly that Revel could not imagine that the wine would spill and run out, that the guests would slowly drift away, and that the players on the patio would grow tired. So the wizard did not speak the name..."

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "of this house as it is. He spoke the name of this house as it would become, saying: Wide lawns gone askew. Hanging lanterns flicker low. A party ending. Lord Endless Ending.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "And in that act of naming, with whatever power and lore this human had at his disposal, the lord of the house looked up and saw that, indeed, it was so. Empty glasses sat on every surface. Already the candles were burning out. A small boat was already in the water, the rowers calling farewell, and the chill of evening entered the air for the first time. That is the moment it has been ever since."

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "From time to time, the grandfather clock chimes, and Lord Endlessly Ending sends another mortal guest down the road. Whether that has been once or a hundred times, who can say?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "At the edges of his vision, just beyond where he can see, despair hovers around the Lord now: not of Revel Beginning, but of an endless ending. Soon he will be alone in an empty, messy house, the best well behind him. That is our host."

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "And that is enough story. For me, I had just one more bowl to smoke, and then I go on to the next of the kingdoms. The next of the houses, I should say." There he falls silent, smiling, and you hear a deep purr emerging from somewhere low in his throat: a self-satisfied sound, utterly independent.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: How long have you been here? What I will say is that me and the halflings stumble up on the last third of that story.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "In truth, I do not know. But I knew that I would not know when I came to this place. I was born in the year of three eclipses, but I do not know if that means anything to you. Like I said, my home is far, far from Tollen and human cities."

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: Does it matter to you to leave before the grandfather clock chimes again?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "That is the question. I very much would not like to test my strength against the Lord, but there are at least two, three... actually, no, four others that I know of. There is a human around here somewhere, not sleeping it off. So I have some time."

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: The guards don't mind if we leave by the road.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "Indeed, they do not. They are not here to guard you, but to guard what sometimes comes down those roads. They are the ones who keep those roads safe. We keep the travelers safe as they go from house to house, like me."

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: We could choose the path of being travelers, going from house to house. In this twilight space.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Indeed. But come, tell me now. What brought you here?

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: You know a Lord Holda.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: No. No. Was he the angry man?

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: So yes, you know our friend, Lord Holda.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "I did not hear the conversation, but I saw the conversation. It was hilarious. You are going to bully a lord in his own manor? He is lucky he made it out, period. Holda sent you to do whatever errand he could not?"

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: Not sure what Holda is up to, to be honest.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "I will offer you one piece of advice in exchange for no keys. Shouting does not work. What is the errand he sent you on?"

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: I would just dish the hard gossip of this Twilight Kingdom.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: I already have decent insight. What's my sense of the sky?

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: Actually, I have pretty good insight.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: You all can do a round of insight checks.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: I mean, I have okay insight.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: I don't think I've rolled, as this character yet, higher than a 5. I rolled a 3.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: Yeah, I rolled at 11.

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: We all rolled terrible insight.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: The rolls are horrible.

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: Oh wait, you know what? I have heroic inspiration. I'm going to roll again.

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: Your life's gotta change sometime?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: 16 or so.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: And less so. Alright.

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: Yep.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Edric. The rest of you are taken with the strangeness of his story and do not quite know what to make of it, or how to get a read on him. There is so much ambiguity. Edric.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: Hold on. I am going to go up to him when he is asking this, almost reach my hand out to pat him on the shoulder, shake him, or whatever is most appropriate, look him in the eye, and ask, "Can we trust you?"

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: he...

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: And then feed that into what I am watching for.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Totally.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: Action.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: You place a hand on his shoulder. He turns and looks up at you through cat eyes that are absolutely unwavering and unblinking. In that moment, your sense is not that he is trustworthy or untrustworthy. It is that he absolutely and entirely keeps his own counsel and goes about his own business, of which you are no part or real concern. Cats can be lovely and affectionate, but every so often a cat will look at you and you understand deeply the utter alienness of that mind, the impossibility of understanding: are you going to sleep on my lap or bite me? I do not mean that in the sense of threat so much as...

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: disinterest.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Disinterest, yes, exactly. You are not just minor characters in his story. By the time it comes for him to use those keys, for whatever purpose he has taken them, he will hardly remember you were the ones he got them from. There is no malevolence there, but you also know not to mistake that for friendship.

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: Mmm.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: You know, we've...

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: But he is not being untruthful. It is almost like it is not worth being untruthful.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: He's not playing with his dinner.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: Have the drunk halflings said or done anything during this entire time?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: The drunk halflings did not make it past the bar. They found a variety of half-empties that they have been hard at work on. You cannot see them, but you can hear them behind the bar by the clattering of glass.

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: What signal does Edric give us?

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: Edric says, "I think he actually rightly understands what we are here for." But he gestures it over. "Txarro or Kaito, maybe one of them could explain it. Or Ayveen. Whoever normally explains these things. Who is smart in the party? I do not remember."

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: Well, Ayveen has the highest intelligence, I think.

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: I guess I do.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: Tarek's pretty smart, too.

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: I have decent intelligence. I will say, "It has been helpful to hear the story of the wizard neighbor and the changing of the nature of the party with the naming. It seems like that was an agreement that was formed. One might even call it a truce. We were told we needed to persuade the Lord to break his truce."

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "Hmm. It is the only bargain struck that I know of."

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: "There is not wanting to break a truce because it was protecting those who needed protecting. This truce, in fact, seems to be forcing the Lord to withdraw his protection where he does not want to. I am motivated to try to persuade him."

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: "None of the mortals that he sends out ever returns to this party. But whether that is good or bad, who can say? And perhaps, having been tricked through cunning into accepting this agreement, bargain, treaty, whatever it is, perhaps having been forced into it through cunning, he will be receptive to ending it." He falls silent and returns to his pipe again.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: Edric browses around.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: As you came through, you cut through the library. There is a ballroom, cellars, a second floor, dining rooms, kitchens. It is a big estate, but the public spaces seem to be bar and buffet, ballroom, library, and all of these outdoor spaces.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: He mentions another human.

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: Person sleeping on the floor in between the couch and the wall.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yeah, he seemed to suggest there was another one besides that, but you haven't seen this other one.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: I'm going to walk around just looking for another human.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: How much later do you all want to go tonight?

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: Mmm...

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: Not much.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: 5 minutes?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: That's perfect.

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: But I'm tired.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: That is perfect. Is there anything else open that you all want to do before wrapping? Because I have a good wrap for that.

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: I guess we'll have to make up some way in which Tarek really enjoyed the party, but things got a little hazy.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: No, I mean, the only thing I was after was looking for this other human.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yep. I am going to say a thing that does not make sense, and I am not going to explain it. You hear the clock strike zero. As you are going through the house looking for this other human, you see, at the far end of the ballroom, in an open door, the Lord of the House, the Lord Endless Ending. He is facing you, taller than the human in front of him, and he has a face that you get the impression is not actually what his face is. There is something older underneath or below a kind of human mask, something wilder, less contained, or less containable.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: Is this the same guy that the owl saw with the, like, weird mask thing?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Precisely. Something unstable, like an unguessed guess in a guessing game, like an unfinished story, like a third act which has not happened. You cannot hear it, but you see him stoop slightly to whisper a word in the ear of a human who has come up to him just after the clock stops striking zero. The human nods, straightens, and hurries out the door. The Lord Endless Ending locks eyes with you across the room and gestures for you to come closer. That is where we will leave it for tonight.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: Just so you know, I am going to telepathically tell my owl familiar to follow the human.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: That's great. That's so good.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: How far away is he?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Maybe seventy or eighty feet from one end of the ballroom to the other.

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: I assume it is completely clear what the notion of treaty refers to at this point?

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: Not everything.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: Kill it now.

lines.speaker: Ayveen
lines.text: We have a small working theory based on our conversation with the tiger-man.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: The Rakshasa was extremely confident that this is what it was, but that does not mean it is.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: Hold on, I am looking at one thing. I have to look it up.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: I mean, it is clear what the treaty was described as. Why it is something we could possibly convince him to break, but he cannot choose to break himself, is completely opaque.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: On that point, in the story, he was challenged to a poetry game, a naming game, where the loser had to accept whatever the winner wanted. Presumably there is something binding to that, at least as the Rakshasa has told it.

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: The Rakshasa is the tiger guy.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Is that a...

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: Sure. I guess Txarro is not convinced about the feasibility.

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: Oh, no.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: A bunch of Tollen misfits winning some kind of poetry contest against a fey lord.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: Not after the.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: Not sure he wants...

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: What?

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: Might, he might want us to win.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: Possibly he wants us to win.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: He did not enter into this thing voluntarily, as far as I can tell. He entered into it...

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: Under duress by some...

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Wizard who bested him.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: He does not have any power to break it whatsoever. He needs somebody clever enough to understand how to break it.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: With some trickery, or I do not know.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: But it doesn't strike me as the kind of thing that he could just break if he's bound by it.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Hmm.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: That is my take, at least. He does not have the ability to break it, but it is not a matter of raw power. The deal he is under is such that he might not even know he wants to break it.

lines.speaker: Txarro
lines.text: We'll find out next time.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yes. Ride along.

lines.speaker: Edric
lines.text: I liked your revelry.
